searchText: I'm going down the path of building my own mock execution JSON-RPC now. I just wanted to reach out in case I was duplicating efforts. cc <@!203220829473996800>. I'm also interested in any IRL implementations, if they're ready. I understand we're all busy though, so no worries if no one is there ☺️ Geth's WIP implementation is here https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23607 Its not 100% confirming to the spec since I am on vacation until tomorrow (only error handling is different) Moving this thread https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/74/files#r714997929 here: Is there any opposition to have the field named as `beneficiary` as per YP and `suggestedBeneficiary` as the name of the corresponding parameter of the `preparePayload` method? cc <@!543900561460822016> <@!291925846556540928> <@!301186049323958275> I prefer `feeRecipient` as that is more clear. I prefer clarity over tradition. `beneficiery` of what? My initial argument was the same, `beneficiary` might be too abstract. Respecting YP looks like a losing argument in this case, I am mostly double checking before submitting PRs with according changes I don't think we should blindly follow the YP without a good reason. That is, I don't think the YP alone is a strong enough argument, especially given how few people actually read it. `feeRecipient` I think conveys the most information about what the field is in the fewest characters. Let me rephrase the original question. Is there any opposition to the following: 1) Rename `feeRecipient` parameter to `suggestedFeeRecipient` of the `engine_preparePayload` parameter set 2) Rename `coinbase` field to `feeRecipient` of the `ExecutionPayload` structure in the Engine API and beacon chain specs <@361447803194441738> I've a work-in-progress mock here: https://github.com/protolambda/mergemock Planning to work on that today/tomorrow, hopefully ready before interop. Note, this channel has been renamed <#692062809701482577> and moved to the "Merge" category ExecutionPayload, has ``` transactions: List[Transaction, MAX_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PAYLOAD] ``` A `Transaction` is `Union[OpaqueTransaction] `and every `OpaqueTransaction` is `ByteList[MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION]` In effect, the spec says that the size of `transactions` can be 16,384 * 1,048,576 bytes. Am i missing something here? There is a discussion here. There is a debate as to where you put safe limits for this (in consensus messages vs as a p2p validation) https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2607#discussion_r711053462

excerpts.author: jmozah
excerpts.content:
ExecutionPayload, has
```
transactions: List[Transaction, MAX_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PAYLOAD]
```
A `Transaction` is `Union[OpaqueTransaction] `and every `OpaqueTransaction` is `ByteList[MAX_BYTES_PER_OPAQUE_TRANSACTION]`

In effect, the spec says that the size of `transactions` can be 16,384 * 1,048,576 bytes.
Am i missing something here?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content:
There is a discussion here.

There is a debate as  to where you put safe limits for this (in consensus messages vs as a p2p validation)
https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2607#discussion_r711053462
